what_its_for: Mobocertinib is a cancer medicine used to treat a type of non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) in adults whose cancer has spread (is advanced or metastatic) and has a specific change in the EGFR gene called an 'exon 20 insertion mutation.' Your doctor will do a test to confirm your cancer has this specific gene change before starting this medicine. It is used when you have already tried at least one platinum-based chemotherapy.
how_to_take: Take mobocertinib by mouth (as a capsule) once daily. You may take it with or without food. Swallow the capsule whole — do not crush, chew, or open it. Try to take it at the same time every day. If you vomit after taking your dose, do NOT take another dose that day — just take your next scheduled dose at the usual time.
dosing: The usual adult dose is 160 mg (four 40 mg capsules) taken by mouth once every day. Your doctor may lower your dose or temporarily stop treatment if you experience certain side effects. Always follow the exact dose your doctor prescribed and do not change it on your own.
missed_dose: If you miss a dose and it has been LESS than 12 hours since your scheduled time, take it as soon as you remember. If it has been MORE than 12 hours, skip the missed dose and take your next dose at your regular scheduled time. Never take two doses at the same time to make up for a missed one.
storage: Store mobocertinib capsules at room temperature between 68°F and 77°F (20°C to 25°C). Keep the capsules in the original container with the lid tightly closed. Protect them from moisture and heat. Keep this medicine out of reach of children and pets. Do not flush unused medicine down the toilet — ask your pharmacist about a medicine take-back program.
what_to_avoid: Avoid grapefruit, grapefruit juice, and Seville oranges (sometimes found in marmalades) while taking this medicine, as they can increase the amount of drug in your body and raise the risk of side effects. Avoid taking antacids, proton pump inhibitors (such as omeprazole or pantoprazole), or H2 blockers (such as famotidine or ranitidine) without first talking to your doctor, as they may reduce how well mobocertinib works. Avoid starting any new prescription, over-the-counter medicines, vitamins, or herbal supplements without checking with your doctor or pharmacist first, as many medicines can interact with mobocertinib. Avoid prolonged sun exposure and use sunscreen, as your skin may be more sensitive.
when_to_call_doctor: Contact your doctor right away or go to the emergency room if you experience: new or worsening shortness of breath, difficulty breathing, or a new cough (these could be signs of a serious lung problem called interstitial lung disease or pneumonitis); fast, irregular, or pounding heartbeat, dizziness, or fainting (signs of a heart rhythm problem called QTc prolongation); severe diarrhea, diarrhea that does not improve, or diarrhea with blood; signs of dehydration such as feeling very thirsty, dry mouth, urinating less than usual, or feeling dizzy; severe nausea or vomiting; skin rash, peeling, or blistering; numbness, tingling, or pain in your hands or feet; or any other new or unusual symptoms that concern you.
when_it_works: It varies from person to person. Some patients may notice improvements in symptoms such as less shortness of breath or coughing within a few weeks. However, it may take several months for your doctor to measure how well the medicine is working through imaging scans (like CT scans). Do not stop taking it on your own even if you do not feel different right away — continue taking it exactly as prescribed and keep all of your follow-up appointments.
special_populations: Pregnancy and breastfeeding: Mobocertinib can harm an unborn baby. If you can become pregnant, use effective birth control during treatment and for at least 1 month after your last dose. If you are a male with a female partner who can become pregnant, use effective birth control during treatment and for at least 1 week after the last dose. Do not breastfeed during treatment and for at least 1 week after your last dose. Kidney or liver problems: Tell your doctor if you have kidney or liver disease, as your dose may need to be adjusted. Older adults: Older adults may be more sensitive to side effects — report any new symptoms to your doctor promptly. Children: This medicine is not approved for use in children.
